builder_plan.scenario: A support or data assistant repeats work across related customer requests.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's memory change in a replay of past tasks, with separate memory per customer.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current memory pipeline plus a no-memory control using the same agent.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, stale memories, retrieval misses, response latency, and all memory maintenance costs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: TrawMem: Reframing Agent Memory as Task-Oriented Role-Adaptive Workspaces
summary: TrawMem replaces query-relevance-based memory retrieval (as in SimpleMem-style systems) with task-oriented workspaces in which memories are assigned roles and jointly selected to include complementary, weakly-related items. It costs additional pipeline complexity: interaction histories must be organized into local threads and a role-assignment and joint-selection step must run per task, adding preprocessing and orchestration overhead, though retrieved context is slightly smaller. It can fail if role assignment misclassifies a memory's function, if thread construction fragments relevant history, or if the reported gains do not transfer beyond the LoCoMo and MemGallery conversational benchmarks to the reader's workload.
rationale: The method is API- and small-model-compatible and reduces context tokens, but its gains are measured only on two conversational memory benchmarks, so it warrants workload-specific validation rather than direct production adoption.

claims.statement: TrawMem replaces query-relevance-based memory retrieval (as in SimpleMem-style systems) with task-oriented workspaces in which memories are assigned roles and jointly selected to include complementary, weakly-related items. It costs additional pipeline complexity: interaction histories must be organized into local threads and a role-assignment and joint-selection step must run per task, adding preprocessing and orchestration overhead, though retrieved context is slightly smaller. It can fail if role assignment misclassifies a memory's function, if thread construction fragments relevant history, or if the reported gains do not transfer beyond the LoCoMo and MemGallery conversational benchmarks to the reader's workload.

Macro-F1 gains of 2.23-3.14 points on LoCoMo and MemGallery across four backbones; on LoCoMo, LLM-Judge scores improve over SimpleMem by 4.07 and 4.31 percentage points (Qwen3.5-9B, DeepSeek-V4-Flash) while using about 12.8% and 5.1% fewer context tokens.
